programs.name: grm
programs.purpose: Estimate refractor velocity and depth from forward and reverse refraction arrival times using the generalized reciprocal method.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: GRM - Generalized Reciprocal refraction analysis for a single layer

params.name: v0
params.description: Weathering-layer velocity in meters per second.

params.name: abtime
params.description: A-to-B travel time in milliseconds; zero selects the last forward arrival time.

params.name: xy
params.description: Override the selected XY distance in meters. The code accepts lowercase xy, despite uppercase XY in the selfdoc, and truncates xy/(2*dx) to an integer half-offset.

params.name: xymax
params.description: Maximum XY distance searched in meters. The code accepts lowercase xymax, despite XYmax in the selfdoc.

params.name: depthres
params.description: Horizontal increment in meters for the dip-correction tangent search.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The smoothness and slope calculations accumulate floats in loop order; close smoothness values can change the selected offset. Float expressions mix with double constants and double-precision sqrt, fabs, atan and cos before assignment to floats. The dip correction searches discrete positions and selects the smallest residual. Invalid or degenerate input can cause out-of-bounds access, division by zero, invalid square roots, or use of uninitialized values; scanf results are not checked. Offset conversions truncate toward zero.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program combines offset optimization, velocity estimation and a discrete geometric tangent search with sensitive numerical edge cases.

test_cases.description: Search for the optimum XY and derive A-to-B time from the final forward arrival.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=24 ntr=1 | suascii bare=1 | awk 'NF {i++; printf "%d 100 %g %g\n", (i-1)*10, 20+(i-1)*5, 135-(i-1)*5}' | grm nt=24 dx=10 v0=500 abtime=0 xymax=40 depthres=1

test_cases.description: Use an explicit A-to-B time and override XY with a value truncated to an available half-offset.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=24 ntr=1 | suascii bare=1 | awk 'NF {i++; printf "%d %g %g %g\n", (i-1)*10, 100+(i-1)*0.1, 20+(i-1)*5, 135-(i-1)*5}' | grm nt=24 dx=10 v0=500 abtime=135 xymax=60 xy=25 depthres=0.5

programs.license_note: The credits cite D. Palmer's 1982 SEG book on the generalized reciprocal method.
